name: MDBM
tagline: Yahoo's memory-mapped, zero-copy key-value library, a heavily tuned descendant of SGI's DBM.
description: MDBM is a C/C++ key-value library that keeps its hash table in a memory-mapped file, so reads can hand back pointers straight into the mapping without copying. Yahoo ran it in production for more than a decade before open-sourcing it under the BSD license in 2014; it descends from Larry McVoy's SGI rewrite of sdbm and adds performance work, multiple locking modes, large-object support, command-line tools, tests and thorough documentation. It suits read-mostly lookup data shared by many processes on one host. The last tagged release is v4.13.0 (December 2018); since then only the original maintainer's fork has seen occasional fixes, so treat it as maintenance-only.
statusNote: Last release v4.13.0 (Dec 2018); the Yahoo repo is idle and only the maintainer's fork (timrc-git/mdbm) saw fixes through 2023.

scale.notes: Single-host, file-backed hash; sized by available address space and page cache.

strengths: Zero-copy reads directly from the memory-mapped file
Shared safely by many processes on one host via its locking modes
Over a decade of production use at Yahoo before open-sourcing
Unusually complete documentation and CLI tooling for a KV library
weaknesses: No transactions or crash-consistent multi-key updates
Single-host only; no replication or network protocol
useCases: Read-heavy lookup tables shared across worker processes
Local caches of configuration or ad/serving metadata
Replacing ndbm/gdbm in C and C++ services
notIdealFor: Workloads needing transactions or durability guarantees
